overall_assessment: Reviewed all 28 packet entries, including every displayed plan and removed span; some plans are capped by the packet. Semester headings are removed without confirmed loss of course content, but staff names survive in six suspects and offering years survive in two. Most name_like flags are false alarms from titles, organisations, subject-matter names and reference authors, and the phone flag is the attachment identifier 32539747 in a reading-list URL; none of the eight random controls has a confirmed anonymization defect.

findings.description: Institutional staff remain identifiable in six suspects (courses 1, 4, 12, 13, 14 and 20). Surviving contexts include labelled teachers, track responsibility, supervision and course/research leadership in prose: [name], [name] and [name], the quoted teacher list, [name], [name], and [name] and [name]. These are people named in institutional roles, rather than literature authors or historical subject matter, and must be removed. The name_like flags therefore include real leaks as well as numerous false positives; no random control shows this defect.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: R/anonymize.R has no AHO handler. The generic staff-role vocabulary omits lærer/lærere, underviser/undervisere, kursansvarlig and track responsibility, and the inline matcher does not cover course leadership expressed as 'will be led by', research 'led by', or 'Supervised by Professor'. The same staff member can consequently survive both a label and a prose mention.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AHO handler or narrowly scoped generic staff patterns for 'Lærere:', 'Flere undervisere:', 'Track responsible:', 'foreleser og kursansvarlig er', course/research leadership 'led by', and 'Supervised by Professor', consuming coordinated name lists and parenthesized roles. Remove only the staff names or complete staff-only lines, preserving surrounding course/research descriptions and reading-list authors. Verify all six affected packet entries, including repeated prose mentions of [name].

findings.evidence: In 2023 the course will focus on games and game-technologies.
findings.description: Two course descriptions retain offering dates despite having no admin_date pre-pass flag. The quoted year dates an annual course theme; course 4 also retains 'In the fall of 2024' when describing a previous Re-Store offering. These are administrative course/semester dates under the rubric, distinct from the historical building dates, publication years and subject-matter event years that should remain.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: The generic season pattern expects the season next to its year and misses the intervening 'of' in 'fall of 2024'. Administrative-year removal is keyword-based and does not recognize the offering-specific construction 'In 2023 the course will focus'. The pre-pass similarly misses these prose forms.
findings.suggested_fix: Recognize English semester-year expressions with optional 'of' before the year, retaining the existing guards for references and subject matter. Add a targeted rule for 'In <year> the course will focus' that drops the year-bearing introductory phrase while retaining the course theme. Extend the audit pre-pass to these contexts and verify that historical events, publication years and the course-series origin statement remain intact.
